nodes.description: A working session is ending. This chapter is reflexive — it models the agent's own close-out obligation under the DWS Learning Standard (EU AI Act Art. 14, human oversight), enforced at runtime by .claude/hooks/session-stop.sh. Unlike Chapters 1-8 it governs no customer-facing domain; the subject is the session itself.

Hook check H4 — the conservative substantive classifier. A session counts as substantive if it touched src/, a .ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.py/.sh file, a *STANDARD*.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, a new agent, or a whitepaper. Dependency, lockfile, .env and .gitignore-only diffs are stripped out first, so a pure dep bump is not substantive. Deliberately conservative: it would rather let a borderline session through than trap a trivial one.
Terminal — classifier found nothing substantive (dep bump, config-only, lockfile). No capture is required and none is faked. Producing a field note here would be noise, not oversight.

The session is substantive but genuinely needs no capture. Three hatches exist, and they are NOT equivalent in auditability: H2 ([skip-learning] / [trivial] / [no-learn] in the commit message) and the standard's own 'N/A — <reason>' line inside a dated field note both leave a durable record in the repo; H1 (DWS_SKIP_LEARNING_OUTCOME=1 in the environment) leaves none and is therefore the weakest — it satisfies the hook without telling any future reader why. Prefer a recorded hatch. An exemption still routes through LEARN_GATE; it does not skip it.
Learning Standard step 1 — update the knowledge base (kb/raw/{articles,signals,repos,images}/), linking to the commits, PRs or docs the session produced.

Step 2 — docs/field-notes/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md: what happened, the insight, next steps, and any HIC decision needed. This is the artefact the hook actually looks for (H3), and the one a human reads. A summary of the diff is not a field note; the insight is the point.

Step 3 — render to Learn/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.html via scripts/render-doc.sh. Self-contained HTML with Base64-embedded images per the Downloadable HTML Rule. Note the real dependency: the script needs pandoc, which is absent from fresh cloud containers and needs sudo to install — if it is unavailable, say so rather than reporting a render that did not happen.

pandoc (or another required tool) is unavailable in this environment. Fail loud per Discipline rule 12: render by an alternative route and say which was used, or record the step as 'N/A — <reason>'. Never claim scripts/render-doc.sh ran when it did not.

Step 4 — export a copy to Google Drive. The repo stays source of truth; Drive holds a generated copy. Frequently 'N/A — Drive MCP not connected in this session', which is a legitimate recorded skip, not a silent omission.

Step 5 — ask the HIC exactly one real, decision-shaped question: a choice they can actually make, with a recommendation and its tradeoff. 'Does this look good?' is not a decision question. For Claude Code this is a synchronous gate; OpenCode may queue it to the field note with Status: PENDING_REVIEW for async batch review.
Step 6 — put every dated commitment in Google Calendar, including derived dates (a 3-month validity implies a follow-up date). 'N/A — no dated commitment arose' is a valid recorded outcome.

The completion gate. Unlike Chapters 1/2/5/6/8 this is NOT an approval gate — nothing outbound is being authorized. It is a gate on finishing: the session may not be declared over until a field note OR a Learn/ HTML dated today exists (hook check H3), or a recorded exemption is in place. Verifies the artefacts are actually on disk and dated today; the hook checks `ls docs/field-notes/$TODAY-*.md` and `ls Learn/$TODAY-*.html`, so a note written under yesterday's date does not satisfy it.

The gate found no dated artefact and no recorded exemption. Return to the steps and produce the minimum. Note the hook's H0 circuit breaker: it sets stop_hook_active and will not block a second time, so a session CAN exit without capture on a retry — which means honouring this node is the agent's responsibility, not something the hook can guarantee. A bypass is not permission.
Terminal — reachable only through LEARN_GATE. The session is over and the HIC has a human-readable capture of what changed, or a recorded reason why none was needed.
